findings.passage: I came to the conclusion that we have to do something. There have been far too many school shootings. There has been far too much gun violence in our streets. And so background checks and the extreme risk protection orders made sense to make sure that we are addressing these where we can.
findings.note: Quoted in a local TV story (Valley News Live) explaining his position on background checks and extreme-risk orders in the 2023 public safety omnibus.

findings.passage: There are a lot of concerns around ghost guns and straw purchases, and background checks will help us address that issue.
findings.note: Quoted by the same TV story on why he backed background checks; mentions home-made guns and straw purchases.

findings.passage: I think they know that when we are considering these types of legislation, we can be gun owners and we can have the traditions that we have while doing the things that we need to do to keep our kids safe.
findings.note: Quoted by the same TV story on how gun owners in his district can accept the new measures.

findings.passage: Since being elected to the State Senate, I have been clear in my opposition to a Gun Storage Law. That has not changed. In Northern Minnesota, we are responsible gun owners and do not need an unenforceable law to tell us how to keep ourselves safe or how to handle our guns.
findings.note: Statement issued in his name, reported by the Ely Echo, opposing a safe-storage requirement for guns in 2024.

findings.passage: Unlike other proposals to keep guns out of the hands of dangerous individuals, this year's legislation surrounding storage of firearms could jeopardize the ability of my law-abiding constituents to protect themselves or their families in an emergency,
findings.note: Quoted in the Ely Echo; says why he opposed the 2024 safe-storage proposal, contrasting it with other proposals on keeping guns from dangerous people.
